details:
I don't see a good reason for VRChat's servers to know the name of an avatar when I view avatar details of a locally built SDK Test Avatar, this is a privacy concern to me.

If the name of the SDK Test Avatar is theoretically something like "Robot for [person's full name]" locally for a commission before upload, that could create a compliance issue when that person's personal data may be leaked to VRChat servers involuntarily/without expectation.

1. Navigate to My Avatars, then to the SDK Test Avatar category.

2. Click on an avatar.

3. Press "View Avatar Details" on your SDK Test Avatar.

4. Check the logs. You'll find a HTTP request for a `local:sdk_<avatar name>` avatar.

```

2026.04.21 09:24:20 Error      -  [API] [150, 404, Get, -1 https://api.vrchat.cloud/api/1/avatars/local:sdk_zeropoly] Abandoning request, because - Avatar Not Found

2026.04.21 09:24:20 Debug      -  [AssetBundleDownloadManager] Starting download of Avatar @ unknown MB, 0 still queued.

2026.04.21 09:24:20 Debug      -  [AssetBundleDownloadManager] [103] Unpacking Avatar (SDK: zeropoly by )

```

2026.04.21 09:00:55 Error      -  [API] [133, 400, Get, -1 https://api.vrchat.cloud/api/1/avatars/local:sdk_Tutorial_Avatar_Robot_v1 (1 light)] Abandoning request, because - "malformed url"

title: Viewing avatar details of a local SDK Test Avatar tries to fetch (non-existent) avatar details from the VRChat API (metadata information leak)
